canonical_claim: DiskObjectStorage::prepareRead serves inline or mutable bytes from memory and uses the standard object-storage read pipeline plus a bounded FileView stage for blob payload windows. Additionally, The generic `ReadPipeline` FileView stage exposes a payload window `[left_bound, right_bound)` as a standalone file and translates downstream positions and right bounds by `left_bound`. Additionally, `DiskObjectStorage::prepareRead` supports the CAS read path by exposing a payload window inside a shared blob through the standard gather, cache, and prefetch chain. Additionally, `ReadPipeline` provides `needFileView`, `FileViewStage`, and `wrapFileView` as a byte-window stage between prefetch and decryption, translating positions and right bounds for files stored as payload windows inside shared CAS blobs.; `readBlobPayload` issues a ranged read over `[0, offset + length)` and exposes only `[payload_offset, payload_end)` through `ReadBufferFromFileView`.
Snapshot-run consumers use streaming reads with fixed linear-scan requests of `head`, tail `get`, and forward-only `getStream`, retaining only the footer index and one block.
`getStream` is permitted only for write-once objects such as runs and seals; mutable objects remain on `get`.
`ObjectStorageBackend::get` converts a concurrent-delete `NoSuchKey` or 404 during GET into `std::nullopt`, matching `CasInMemoryBackend`.

CA data-part reads consult in-flight transaction objects before committed metadata, providing read-your-writes for staged projection sub-parts. Additionally, Disk transactions need a read-your-writes API for files and directories staged inside the transaction so later MergeTree code can inspect staged state without committing and reopening the transaction. Additionally, The in-flight disk-transaction interface provides default no-op methods `tryGetInFlightStorageObjects`, `tryReadFileInFlight`, `tryGetInFlightFileSize`, `hasInFlightDirectory`, and `listInFlightDirectory`. Additionally, The in-flight methods `tryGetInFlightStorageObjects`, `tryReadFileInFlight`, `tryGetInFlightFileSize`, `hasInFlightDirectory`, and `listInFlightDirectory` forward the read-your-writes overlay to the metadata transaction and remain part of the transaction interface. Additionally, `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::exists`, `existsFile`, and `existsDirectory` consult in-flight staging for a part being assembled. Additionally, `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::iterate` merges committed and staged entries through `DataPartStorageMergedIterator` so `loadProjections` can iterate a staged projection directory. Additionally, `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::getFileSize`, `getRemotePaths`, `prepareRead`, and `readFileIfExists` resolve in-flight sources, including staged blobs and inline mutable bytes before commit.; An open CA transaction has a single mutable view: reads combine the overlay with committed state and observe preceding writes, renames, and deletes from the same transaction.; Commit `1f3685a81f3` added reading from a transaction's own uncommitted state so transactional disks could inspect their own writes instead of committing and starting a new transaction.
A cold `resolveRef` shard read costs one `HEAD` and one `GET`, while a warm single-flight resolution costs zero additional operations.
The shard decode TTL applies only to present entries; absence is never TTL-cached.
Strict-freshness callers such as the publish gate pass `allow_stale = false` and always issue a shard `HEAD` regardless of `shard_decode_cache_ttl_ms`.

A part-manifest open costs one manifest `HEAD` and zero or one `GET` depending on the `(ManifestId, token)` decode-cache result. Additionally, The `(ManifestId, Token)` cache is safe because part manifests are immutable content-addressed objects, and a cache hit avoids a manifest `GET`. Additionally, `CasManifestReader` keys its decode cache by `(ManifestId, Token)` and performs a mandatory HEAD even on a cache hit to prove existence and obtain the token. Additionally, A manifest-cache hit still performs a `HEAD`; this deliberate fail-closed tradeoff removes the GET and decode but not the round trip, and a blob-backed open costs at least two `HEAD`s, up to two control `GET`s, and one blob `GET`.

A CAS MergeTree read routes inline entries to memory, blob-backed files to ranged S3 GETs, and verbatim files to plain `IObjectStorage::readObject` without CAS indirection.; A CAS read resolves a ref, reads a manifest, locates an entry, and either decodes inline bytes or performs a ranged GET over the blob payload; inline entries require no additional object-store operation.; The CAS read path parses a disk path with `Parts/PartPathParser`, resolves the ref table to a manifest, and reads either stored blob objects or inline manifest bytes.
The blob-backed read sequence is `resolveRef → readManifest → lookupPath → getBlobViewPlan → readBlobPayload → ReadBufferFromFileView`.
`resolveRef` hashes the ref name with `shardOf(ref_name)`, reads one root shard, and returns `std::nullopt` on a missing ref rather than throwing `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.
When a control object disappears between `HEAD` and `GET`, `Backend::get` returns `std::nullopt`; callers that require presence convert that absence to `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.
Column pruning is structural: the MergeTree reader requests only needed files, and CA performs per-file `lookupPath` and ranged reads.
`Placement::Inline` entries are served from decoded manifest memory through `ReadBufferFromOwnMemoryFile` with zero S3 operations.
A shard decode cache entry is keyed by the shard key and stores `{token, shard, validated_at}`; a token match means the decoded root shard remains valid.
Single-flight shard reads bound concurrent GETs for one shard to one, regardless of query concurrency.

For committed projections, `existsDirectory("<uuid>/<part>/<proj>.proj")` checks for a manifest key with the `<proj>.proj/` prefix and `listDirectory` strips that prefix from child names.; `PartFolderView::listChildren` collapses the first path component over manifest entries and non-reserved mutable files, including projection-directory listings.; Committed projection discovery requires `existsDirectory` and `listDirectory` projection-subdirectory branches that collapse `<proj>.proj/*` to one `<proj>.proj` entry when listing the parent part.

The file cache is write-around rather than write-through: the first read after upload can miss once, then immutable content-hash data is cached without an invalidation hazard.; Write-through caching and caching the refs/manifests control plane are out of scope; immutable-blob write-around is the intended design.

`PartFolderView` is an immutable no-I/O snapshot containing a resolved ref, copied mutable files, and the same `shared_ptr<const PartManifest>` held by the store manifest cache; mutable refreshes create a new view sharing that manifest pointer. Additionally, `PartFolderView` contains `PartRefKey`, `ManifestId`, encoded manifest size, publication time, copied mutable files, and the shared immutable manifest pointer; its query surface is pure and index-free. Additionally, `PartFolderView` is immutable and joins `RootNamespace`, `ref_name`, resolved `RootRef` payload, decoded `PartManifest`, a file index, and a directory/projection index.; `PartFolderView` never calls back into metadata storage, never mutates `Cas::Store`, and performs no object-store I/O; `Cas::Store` does not depend on the facade.
`PartFolderView::fileSize` reports mutable value length, inline byte length, or blob size according to the matching file representation; `inlineBytes` returns bytes only for inline entries.
In Phase 2, `getView` always calls `readManifestShared`, including `CachedForLoad`, `ForceFresh`, and `StrictValidate`; there is no retained view state yet.
The facade read API consists of `getView`, `resolve`, and `existsRef`; `getView` returns `nullptr` for an absent ref, while `resolve` performs ref-only access without reading a manifest.
After a retained view is refreshed solely because `mutable_files` drifted while `manifest_id` stayed equal, no manifest `HEAD` or `GET` is required.

`Freshness::CachedForLoad` resolves with `allow_stale=true` and may serve or retain a validated view; `ForceFresh` resolves with `allow_stale=false`, never serves a retained view, and may update a view after body validation; `StrictValidate` resolves fresh, never serves a retained view, and never retains a result. Additionally, `Freshness::CachedForLoad` uses stale-tolerant ref resolution, `Freshness::ForceFresh` uses fresh resolution for mutable and write-source paths, and `Freshness::StrictValidate` bypasses retained views for fresh validated reads.

The normative `getView` algorithm first resolves the ref, returns `nullptr` for absence without retaining it, validates a retained view for `CachedForLoad`, builds through `readManifestShared` on a miss, retains only eligible non-strict results, and then returns the view.; With caching enabled, `getView` checks an active slot and shared map, resolves the ref, reads and validates the `PartManifest`, builds the view, and publishes it only if local cache state still matches.
A `CachedForLoad` retained hit has no remote manifest operation; a mutable-only drift clones the view around the shared decode, while a changed manifest causes a validation mismatch and rebuild.

The method-routing contract uses `resolve(ForceFresh)` for mutable files and ref stamps, `getView(CachedForLoad)` for ordinary content, directories, storage objects, inline bytes, and blob plans, and `getView(ForceFresh)` for part-manifest export and write-source evidence.

`getStorageObjectsIfExist` is a dedicated one-lookup override that avoids the inherited `existsFile` plus `getStorageObjects` two-read path.; Phase 2 overrides `getStorageObjectsIfExist` to use one routed lookup for in-part paths, fixes `getFileSize` to use one routed resolve, and fixes `existsFileOrDirectory` to use one view query for committed in-part paths.
The read path remains a body GET by content key at a constant blob_header_len offset and never consults .meta.
